overview: This Senate resolution condemns the Chinese government for what it calls transnational repression, meaning efforts by a government to reach across borders to spy on, harass, threaten or pressure people living abroad, including in the United States. It points to targeting of dissidents, human rights defenders, Uyghurs, Tibetans and Hongkongers, Hong Kong arrest warrants and bounties for people overseas, and pressure on their relatives still in China. The resolution states that everyone living in the U.S. has the right to be free of foreign government intimidation and supports U.S. efforts to investigate and hold accountable those involved. It expresses the Senate's view and does not create new laws or penalties. As of October 30, 2025, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate's calendar, meaning it is eligible for a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say the resolution sends a clear message that foreign intimidation of people living in the United States will not be tolerated and backs efforts to protect targeted communities.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending, so it adds no new tools to stop the harassment it describes.
